name: TiXel
summary: Shopify app for Meta and TikTok pixels, with unlimited pixels, product-level scoping and server-side Events API tracking on one flat plan.
best_for: Shopify merchants running Meta and TikTok ads who need more than the free channel apps give them: several pixels on one store, pixels scoped to individual products, or server-side Events API tracking alongside the browser pixel to recover events that ad-blockers and Safari strip
skip_if: you run one pixel for one brand, since Shopify's Meta and TikTok channels do that for nothing; or you cannot put real traffic through the store inside the one-day trial, because the reported failure is a pixel that installs cleanly and then tracks nothing
honest_knock:
The rating is the most useful number on this listing, but not for the reason an average usually is. Read on 18 September 2026 it is 4.6 across 93 reviews, and the shape behind it is 84 five-star, 3 four-star, nothing at three or two, and 6 one-star. A month earlier it was 4.1 across 78, with 7 at the bottom. Nothing sits in the middle on either reading. That is not a mediocre product; it is a binary one: it works immediately, or it installs cleanly and then tracks nothing at all.

The one-star reviews describe the same failure in the same words: the pixel is set up by the instructions, no page views or add-to-carts ever arrive, and support does not reply. We cannot verify what happened in any individual account, but the consistency of the complaint is itself information.

What is new since August is that the developer now answers them in public. A reply dated 2 September 2026 attributes the empty data to manual pixel configuration, where one mismatched ID or event setting is enough to stop events being recorded at all, and says that step is no longer needed: TiXel now integrates officially with Meta and TikTok and links the pixel to your ad account automatically. That is the vendor's account of its own worst reviews, so treat it as a claim to test rather than a fix to trust. It is at least a specific and checkable one, but the trial has shrunk to a single day (it was seven in September), which leaves very little room to check it before you are billed. On 2 November 2026 the record stood at 106 reviews, with 97 five-star and 5 one-star.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Unlimited Plan · per month, or $119.94 a year at a stated 50% saving, on a one-day trial
pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-11-02 on apps.shopify.com/tixel) One paid plan and no ladder to climb, and the amounts are unchanged since 22 August 2026. Unlimited Plan is $19.99 a month, or $119.94 a year at a stated 50% saving, and carries unlimited pixels, server-side Events API pixels, regular pixels via pixel code, pixels scoped to specific products, automatic event triggers with no manual event configuration, accurate tracking and online support. One term has changed again and it matters: the free trial is now one day, where the listing advertised seven in September and three in August. The other tier, Development Stores, is still free but only for development and partner stores, with billing activated on upgrade — the same shape as this developer's Blocky listing. Charges are in USD and recur every 30 days. Developer Effective Apps, 13 Max Nordau, Ashdod, Israel; the app launched 19 October 2020. The review record has moved a long way: 106 reviews at 4.8 on 2 November 2026, up from 93 at 4.6 in September and 78 at 4.1 in August, distributed 97 five-star, 4 four-star, none at three or two, and 5 one-star.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session installed TiXel (TiXel Multi Pixels in the admin) on a Shopify development store. The app opened on a plan choice with a Yearly and a Monthly plan and a trial of one day, and the Shopify approval screens asked for a payment method, so no pixel was added. The app was uninstalled; nothing was paid. Install: the install form was sent at about 22:38; the dialog Install app for TiXel Multi Pixels by Effective Apps asked for customer data, staff data and store data. The app opened at about 22:39 on Welcome to TiXel Multi Pixels. Core action NOT DONE: the app asks for a plan first and Shopify asks for a payment method for it. No pixel ID was entered, no Meta or TikTok connection was made and no event overview was seen. Plans in the app: Yearly Plan $9.99/month billed annually (Sale: Save 50%) and Monthly Plan $19.99/month billed monthly, both with Add Unlimited Pixels, 1-click automatic TikTok Pixel creation, 1-click automatic Meta Pixel connection, the Conversion API for server side tracking and automatic event triggers; each store gets at most 1 trial day altogether. No free Development plan was offered. Checkout: the yearly plan opened the Shopify screen Approve subscription: Annual Unlimited Plan, $119,94 USD every year, a 1-day free trial ending on 18 Nov, total $119,94 due 18 Nov, the row Add payment method and a greyed out Approve. The monthly plan showed Monthly Unlimited Plan, $19,99 USD every 30 days with the same trial and row. The line You will not be billed for this test charge was NOT on either screen, so nothing was approved and no card was entered. Cancelling: no subscription existed. Settings, Apps, Uninstall opened Uninstall TiXel Multi Pixels? which warns that data managed by the app will be deleted, says a request goes to the developer within 48 hours to delete personal customer information, and needs a reason (Testing multiple apps). Clean up: the app was uninstalled and is gone from Installed; no theme or product change. Our own tab was closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The trial lasts only one day per store, the app shows nothing before a plan is approved, and both approval screens needed a payment method with no test charge line.
